project.name: AI Search Landing
project.summary: A product-led SaaS landing page for an AI search product that helps knowledge workers and small teams find answers across scattered work documents.

diagnosis.raw_request: 帮我做一个 AI 搜索产品官网
main_gaps: No conversion goal or CTA was specified.
No product proof, screenshots, metrics, or integration list was provided.
No brand voice, visual tone, or design system was provided.
No responsive, accessibility, or content constraints were provided.
risk: Without assumptions, a generator may produce a generic AI landing page.
Unsupported logos, metrics, or certifications must not be invented.

audience.primary_user: knowledge workers and small teams that search across scattered work documents
audience.secondary_user: team leads evaluating productivity tools for fast-moving internal teams
audience.context_of_use: Visitors arrive after hearing about the product and need to understand whether it can search across their work tools without setup friction.
pain_points: Important answers are buried across documents, chats, tickets, and shared drives.
Teams waste time asking repeat questions because source material is hard to find.
Generic AI search claims do not prove whether the product fits real workflows.
jobs_to_be_done: Understand what the product searches and how answers are grounded.
Decide whether to start a trial or request a demo.
Trust that the product is secure enough for work knowledge.

goals.design_goal: make the value of cross-workspace AI search clear in the first screen while building enterprise trust
goals.conversion_goal: convert qualified visitors into trial signups or demo requests

message.core_claim: Find trusted answers across every work document in seconds.
supporting_points: Connect common work tools and search across them from one place.
Show answer sources so teams can verify results.
Help small teams reduce repeat questions and knowledge bottlenecks.
proof_points: Product surface showing a question, sourced answer, and linked documents.
Integration row for docs, chat, tickets, and drives.
Security section covering permissions-aware search and admin controls.
content_warnings: Avoid vague AI slogans without concrete product behavior.
Do not imply customer logos, metrics, or certifications that are not provided.

section_details.purpose: Explain the product promise immediately and show a realistic sourced-answer product surface.
section_details.visual_anchor: Search answer panel with linked source documents

section_details.purpose: Name the cost of scattered work knowledge without overexplaining.
section_details.visual_anchor: Lightweight split showing docs, chats, tickets, and drives

section_details.purpose: Connect the AI search value to concrete user actions.
Show the path from question to trusted answer.
Make the search coverage feel practical while avoiding fake partner claims.
Build trust before the final CTA.
section_details.visual_anchor: Calm trust panel with clear copy

section_details.purpose: Give qualified visitors a clear next step.

interaction_states: Primary CTA has default, hover, focus, and mobile-visible states.
Secondary demo CTA remains available but visually secondary.
Product mock shows a typed question, answer, source chips, and linked documents.
Mobile layout keeps headline, product surface, and CTA readable without overlap.
interaction_contract: Primary CTA opens a trial signup form or navigates to /signup. It must show default, hover, focus, disabled, loading, success, and error states when implemented.
Secondary CTA opens or scrolls to a product demo section. It must remain visually secondary and have default, hover, focus, and loading states when implemented.
Source chips and linked documents in the product mock are clickable when the target tool supports interactions; otherwise label them as visual-only proof elements.
Integration items are non-clickable placeholders in the golden demo unless real integration URLs are provided.
Failed signup or unavailable demo states should keep the visitor on the page with a clear retry path.
responsive_accessibility: Use desktop >= 1024px, tablet 768-1023px, and mobile <= 767px as target layout bands.
On mobile, stack headline, copy, CTAs, and product surface in that order; keep the primary CTA visible above the fold or repeated after the product proof.
Product mock must resize without horizontal scrolling and keep answer text, source chips, and linked documents readable.
Keyboard tab order follows navigation, primary CTA, secondary CTA, product source links, integrations, security proof, final CTA.
Every interactive element has a visible focus state and at least a 44px touch target on mobile.
Use semantic heading order and descriptive alt text for product mock, source icons, and integration placeholders.

differentiators: real product surface in the hero

strategy_options.name: Enterprise Trust
strategy_options.best_use_case: Best when the product must feel credible for teams evaluating work knowledge and security.
strategy_options.visual_tone: Restrained, product-led, sharp typography, neutral surfaces, restrained blue accents.
strategy_options.information_structure_focus: Lead with value, prove with sourced-answer product UI, then address workflow, integrations, and security.
strategy_options.risk: Can feel too reserved if the product needs a more consumer-facing launch tone.

strategy_options.name: Search Copilot Demo
strategy_options.best_use_case: Best when the page should quickly demonstrate the search interaction.
strategy_options.visual_tone: Interactive, product-forward, slightly more energetic, with a larger live-search mock.
strategy_options.information_structure_focus: Lead with an example question and answer, then explain why the answer is trustworthy.
strategy_options.risk: May over-index on the demo and under-explain business trust.

strategy_options.name: Founder-Led Launch
strategy_options.best_use_case: Best when the product is early and needs a sharper narrative around the problem.
strategy_options.visual_tone: Editorial, direct, sparse, with strong copy and fewer interface panels.
strategy_options.information_structure_focus: Lead with the pain of scattered knowledge, then introduce the product as a focused answer.
strategy_options.risk: Can feel less mature for enterprise buyers if proof and security are too light.

reference_direction.name: AI product landing page
reference_direction.source_boundary: Use product proof, conversion clarity, and trust hierarchy as mechanisms; do not copy third-party brand assets or full DESIGN.md files.

token_summary: Deep ink primary for text and high-trust surfaces.
Restrained blue accent for links, focus, and primary action.
Light neutral backgrounds with low-contrast borders.
8px default radius and restrained card depth.
assumptions: No real logo, customer metrics, or screenshots were provided.
Use realistic product placeholders rather than invented proprietary assets.

accessibility: no text embedded in unreadable imagery

must_avoid: decorative glow as the main visual idea

assumptions: The product is early but credible enough to show a realistic product surface.
The first conversion target is trial signup, with demo as secondary.
open_questions: Which integrations are confirmed for launch?
Are there real screenshots or customer proof points available?
